items.title: Vince Lateano interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: a mutual friend of Cal’s and mine was a great musician/drummer/vibist John Rae

ctx.x: Right. What’s it like trying to absorb the Latin end of things? Because I know you’ve worked with Cal Tjader.

With Cal Tjader. Yeah. Well that was a piece of luck because I was thrown in with Poncho Sanchez and a mutual friend of Cal’s and mine was a great musician/drummer/vibist John Rae. And he’d worked with Cal and he’d worked with Vince Guaraldi and Herbie Mann. He lived out here but he was originally from Boston and spent a lot of time in New York, he’d played with Shearing — played vibes with Shearing — a great musician. And he’s gone. And anyway we were good friends and he told me Cal was looking for somebody, “Do…
If someone says playing merengue as opposed to, I don’t know, a salsa beat, do you know what that means specifically?
